tasks.title: Lane fixture and serial baseline: a sandbox repo with 9 tasks (6 independent, 3 chained by waits_on, 3 editing one shared function), each with a verify command. Serial drive's wall-clock, tasks done, verify pass rate, tokens per task and conflicts are the bar every later step must beat

Load control so lanes do not saturate the machine: a verify semaphore (one full suite at a time), nice/taskpolicy for sessions and verify, process-group kill on verify timeout, a vitest maxWorkers cap (drive-load note 01M3PCDC, fixes 1-5)
Ready frontier: readyTasks honours waits_on (queuedTasks ignores it today, drive-queue.ts:42); `sofar next --ready`; serial drive takes the ready head
Record-root override: a lane session writes the main checkout's .sofar, never its worktree's stale committed copy; lanes never commit .sofar

`sofar drive --lanes N`: a persistent lane worktree pool (deps installed once), tasks as branches, lanes recorded on run_started. `--lanes 1` stays byte-identical to today's run (session-driver D6 holds there)

Coordinator: one process assigns ready tasks to free lanes and records each assignment, so the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task. Budgets (--cost-cap, --max-sessions) count across lanes; a rate-limited lane parks instead of stalling

Serial merge queue: rebase a passing task branch onto the run base, re-verify when the base moved, fast-forward. A conflict becomes a merge handoff to the lane's next session. Affected-tests verify per merge, full suite per batch

Measure local lanes against serial on the 1.1 fixture. Keep only if wall-clock falls ≥40%, duplicate work is 0, tasks done and verify pass rate are no lower, merge-conflict reopens ≤10% and tokens per task rise ≤5%

Region leases at PreToolUse: an Edit's old_string maps to its markdown section or enclosing symbol, else the whole file. An overlap with another lane stops the edit with a reason; the session works elsewhere or parks (WIP commit, write-back, leases released). Older task wins, so no deadlock; union-merge files never lease. NEEDS the operator's ruling on r4-fixes D17 (deny only on an explicit-forbid rule) for driven lanes

Footprint prediction and conflict-aware scheduling: task `touches`, the record's mention index, files earlier sessions on the task touched, git co-change. A free lane takes the first ready task that misses every live lease and footprint, else idles; skipped tasks age up

Context packets, deterministic and one line each: lease notice (who holds what, for which task), change brief on merge (task, regions, diffstat, decisions and memories logged, write-back), park/resume packet (own write-back, WIP sha, the brief it waited for)
Measure conflict-aware lanes against naive lanes: merge-conflict rework sessions, parks, lanes busy, wall-clock. Keep each piece only if it improves on 2.5

Cloud launch and readback without a TTY: `claude --cloud` refuses a non-TTY (r4-fixes M24). Verify a scriptable launch (routines via API call, or a pty), a branch per task, results back through pushed branches (needs the Claude GitHub App on the repo), and session end detected from the branch's record

Cloud lane adapter: a lane is a cloud session on its task branch. The local coordinator polls and fetches, verifies locally, merges through the queue, and `--resume` re-attaches after the laptop sleeps (the record is the queue)
Conflicts in cloud lanes: no edit-time leases (a cloud VM cannot read the local lease store), so scheduling by footprint plus the merge queue. Measure conflict rework against local lanes
Measure cloud lanes against local lanes: wall-clock, cost per task, tasks finished with the laptop closed, verify pass rate

Thread model (D15): a task is a thread, not a session. A retry or a resumed park continues the task's own conversation when the coordinator's resume-or-refresh rule says it pays, else a fresh session takes the 3.3 packet. Each task has an inbox in the record (events addressed to the task id), which hooks deliver at the next tool or prompt boundary. A parked thread is woken only when what it waits on resolves (a lease freed, a dependency merged, CI failed in Phase 4)

Thread cost levers (D15). (a) Shared warm prefix: the session-start injection is byte-identical across lanes with per-session lines last, and lane starts are staggered so lanes 2..N read lane 1's cache. (b) Warm-cache scheduling: resume inside the cache TTL, else refresh. (c) Fork at a checkpoint: a retry forks from the end of exploration, not from the failed attempt. (d) A parked thread holds no process. (e) A batched inbox: an FYI packet waits for the next boundary and never wakes a thread. (f) A per-thread context ceiling that hands off instead of compacting

payload.because: An in-flight lane's work is real and independent of the lane that fired the stop; killing it throws that away and leaves no handoff. Counting launches in flight is the only way --max-sessions stays a bound when N launch at once. The cost cap can only see what has been reported, so the overshoot is stated rather than hidden (session-driver D14 already scopes it to one driver).
payload.chose: 2.3 coordinator: a lanes run (≥2) runs one loop that, each pass, gives every free lane (no live session, not parked) the first ready task no lane holds — in the lane holding its branch, else the next clean free lane — and runs each lane's session → gate → land → handoff as its own job. --max-sessions counts launches in flight; --cost-cap sums every lane's reported cost and is checked before each launch, so up to N-1 running sessions may add to it after it is reached. A stop rule that fires (needs_user, exhausted verify, an unlandable branch, stalls, a budget) launches nothing more and DRAINS: lanes in flight finish, are gated and file their handoffs, then run_stopped; the first stop wins. ^C or --stop signals every live session. Stalls count consecutively in completion order across lanes. A task_done is not credited for a task another lane held during the session. Concurrent launches resolve by the transport's session id; the timestamp fallback sees sibling sessions as candidates and stays unresolved rather than guess (session-driver D3). `--lanes 1` keeps the serial loop.
payload.over: Killing in-flight lanes when a stop rule fires; N independent loops; counting only finished sessions against --max-sessions; folding rebase into 2.3 (a diverged branch still stops the run as error per D20 until 2.4's merge queue)

payload.because: The task asks that the statusline and interactive sessions see which lane holds which task; both read the fold, so the assignment has to be an event. One event with an optional task is the smallest schema that can also free a lane after an unresolved launch.
payload.chose: Each assignment is a new event, `lane_assigned {run, lane: integer ≥1, task?}` on envelope session cli: with task, the coordinator gave that lane that task; without, it freed the lane (a launch that resolved to no session files no handoff to free it). The fold keeps `run.assignments` [{lane, task, ts}], lane order, present only when non-empty: an assignment replaces the lane's and any other lane's hold on the same task, and ends at the handoff for its task, at run_stopped and at run_adopted (the old driver's lanes are gone). Excluded from drift like every driver event (commit-attribution D18). Where the record shows "the task in flight", a lanes run shows what its lanes hold, `L<k> <task>` joined by ", ": describeRun (the injected Driven line and sofar status), the statusline's drive segment, the prompt's drive line and the progress file's `task`.
payload.over: Recording lanes only in the progress file (not the record, invisible to other clones and to the injected digest); a separate lane_released event type; putting the lane on handoff (an unresolved launch files no handoff, so the lane would read held forever)

payload.because: M1: a usage-limited launch looks like an unresolved stall and two stop the run, though nothing is wrong with the work. The stream names the limit and its reset, so the wait is read from a fact, not guessed. Routes can send lanes to different agents, so one lane's limit is not assumed to be every lane's. The serial run's behaviour is pinned byte for byte by 2.2.
payload.chose: A rate-limited lane parks: the claude-code adapter reports a stream `rate_limit_event` whose status is `rejected` on SessionExit.rate_limit {type?, resets_at?}. On a lanes run that launch never counts as a stall; its lane takes no task until the reset the stream names (+30s), or for 5 minutes doubling to 60 per consecutive park when none is named, and the task goes back to the queue for other lanes. A session that registered before the limit still files its handoff. With every lane parked the run waits for the earliest reset, still honouring --stop and ^C. A serial run is unchanged (a limited launch still stalls).
payload.over: Stopping the run on a rate limit; parking every lane on one lane's limit; parking a serial run too; matching stderr prose

payload.because: Concurrent lanes make divergence the common case, so the D20 stop fired on most second landings. A merge left in the lane is finished with only `git add` and `git commit`, which the floor already grants, and its state is a fact git keeps, so the prompt is right on every path (runTask, recover, a resumed run). Rebasing first keeps the base linear for 2.6's bisect; merging a branch that already holds a merge keeps the session's resolution instead of replaying the conflict. A distinct handoff reason is what 2.5's merge-conflict reopen rate is counted from.
payload.chose: 2.4 merge queue: landings run one at a time through a promise-chain queue in the driver. A branch that already contains the base fast-forwards as before, with no re-verify. A branch the base moved past is integrated in its own lane: rebased onto the base tip when it holds no merge commit, else (or when the rebase stops) merged with `git merge --no-edit`. Either way the gate runs again in the lane on the new tree, and a pass fast-forwards the base by compare-and-swap. A merge that stops on conflicts is LEFT IN PROGRESS in the lane: the task is reopened, the session's handoff is the new reason `merge_conflict` with the conflicting paths as its detail, and the lane's next session (the lane holds the branch, and its dirty tree keeps other tasks out) is told by the prompt, read from the lane's MERGE_HEAD and unmerged paths, to resolve, `git add` and `git commit`. A lane still holding unmerged paths at acceptance is never committed: that is a merge conflict again, with no gate. One task's merge_conflict handoffs in a run count against --max-verify-attempts and stop the run as stall when they reach it.
payload.over: Rebase-only with the conflict aborted and the session told to `git rebase` (git rebase is outside the protocol floor, permissions.ts DEFAULT_ALLOW, so a driven session cannot run it, and a rebase in progress detaches HEAD so no lane would hold the branch); keeping the conflict in the record only (a resumed run's recover path has no session to file a handoff for, so the next prompt would lack it); stopping the run on any divergence (D20, D21's stop-until-2.4); rebasing at every launch.
